Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testPropertyOptionGroup()` reveals a problem with the handling of mutually exclusive option groups when default options are supplied as a Properties instance. Specifically, the test sets up two OptionGroups where options "a" and "b" are mutually exclusive in the first group, and "x" and "y" in the second group. The command line arguments specify the option "-a", but the properties specify "b" and "x" as true. According to the current bug report, this situation is allowed by the parser, leading to an inconsistent state where both "a" and "b" (mutually exclusive options) are considered selected.

Inspecting the `Parser.parse()` method shows that after processing command line arguments and options, it calls `processProperties(Properties)`. In the `processProperties` method, each property not already selected by the command line is added to the command line options without checking or updating the state of any OptionGroups. 

The `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option)` method enforces mutual exclusivity by allowing only one option to be selected, throwing an `AlreadySelectedException` if a conflicting option is selected. However, this check and update method is not invoked during the property processing step, meaning the mutually exclusive groups do not get their state updated or checked against default options from Properties.

The root cause is the lack of logic in `Parser.processProperties()` to verify and update the selection state of OptionGroups when default options are added. This results in mutually exclusive options being simultaneously assigned when one option is from the command line and another is from the properties, violating the exclusivity constraint.

Hence, the bug occurs because `processProperties` adds options without consulting or updating the corresponding OptionGroups, unlike the normal command line option processing which would enforce exclusivity. This leads to an inconsistent `CommandLine` state that includes options from the same group selected by both command line arguments and default properties.

No conflicting recent bug reports explicitly address option groups, so the primary evidence is the examined code and the current bug report. The solution likely involves modifying `processProperties` to check for option group conflicts by calling `OptionGroup.setSelected` or similar logic before adding an option from Properties.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
